The GPs who I  originally dealt with were very caring, particularly when I was diagnosed with secondary bone cancer.
However, the changes in staff, the constant restructuring of the NHS and Covid have led me to lose faith in the surgery.
I had a telephone conversation with a GP last Friday,  which wasn't easy as I'd lost my voice. The GP invited me to come to the surgery, but I didn't feel well enough and, as I'm no longer allowed to drive, couldn't face the thought of getting dressed and going out in the rain.
Instead, I was advised that I had a viral infection and was prescribed liquid paracetamol. I'm still waiting for the pharmacy to deliver it. I was also advised that I could contact 111 which seemed a bit OTT to me when I live no more than a mile from the surgery.
Today (Sunday) I  was fed up with constant coughing,  no voice and no sleep, so I did call 111.
